correctness.rationale: On every reset-free leg with initial voltage below the constant-drive equilibrium, voltage is a strictly increasing coordinate. Solving the threshold equation as a function of voltage shows that increasing the initial threshold adds the strictly positive factor \(((V-v)/(V-u))^{1/\tau}\) times the threshold increment at every finite voltage. Hence the first sign-changing threshold crossing, if it exists, occurs at strictly larger voltage. The reset sends a crossing at voltage \(r\) to \((0,r+\Delta)\), so constant forcing lets the one-leg comparison iterate on the reset section. This proves strict ordering of corresponding reset voltages and the finite spike-count monotonicity. Grazing contacts are excluded exactly as in the source reset definition. No numerical experiment substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The result resolves the source paper's full finite spike-count monotonicity question on the natural tonic-drive subfamily, exactly the regime central to Type III phasic firing. It identifies a structural reason the autonomous case is tractable: reset voltages inherit strict threshold order, and autonomy lets that order survive successive resets. It also shows that the source's suggested inequality \(f(v)>v\) is unnecessary in this regime. This is more than a zero-spike restatement or a numerical observation and isolates the forcing phase, rather than the reset itself, as the obstruction to the same induction for nonconstant inputs.
